name: What happens if my bathroom remodel uncovers mold?

mainEntity.name: What happens if my bathroom remodel uncovers mold behind the walls or under the floor?
mainEntity.text: What happens if my bathroom remodel uncovers mold behind the walls or under the floor?

acceptedAnswer.text: If mold is uncovered, the first priority is to stop the moisture source before rebuilding anything. That usually means identifying whether the problem came from a shower leak, failed grout or caulk, a plumbing issue, or poor ventilation. Damaged drywall, insulation, subflooring, or framing may need to be removed and replaced depending on how far the moisture spread. This can affect both the cost and schedule of the remodel. In older bathrooms, mold often appears together with rot or other concealed water damage, which is why contingency budgeting is so important. Homeowners should ask the contractor how these discoveries are documented, who handles the repair scope, and whether specialty remediation is needed. A proper response is not just covering the area back up. The underlying leak or ventilation issue has to be corrected so the new bathroom does not fail again.
acceptedAnswer.description: If mold is found during a remodel, work usually pauses in the affected area while the source of moisture is identified and corrected. The damaged materials may need removal and replacement before rebuilding can continue. Mold is often a sign of a leak or ventilation problem that must be fixed first.
